records.category: payment in full for equipment partly never delivered
records.people: Radoslav Sretenovic (Auditor General of the State Audit Institution, who signed the report); the Vice-Governor of the National Bank of Serbia who set up the commission by decision during the audit (not named in the report); Muhlbauer ID Services GmbH, Germany (foreign supplier)
records.summary: Serbia's State Audit Institution, in its audit of the National Bank of Serbia for financial year 2012 (report 400-264/2013-01, Belgrade, 12 December 2013), drew attention to equipment bought in 2007 under two contracts between the Ministry of the Interior, the National Bank of Serbia and the German supplier Muhlbauer ID Services GmbH. Under a 2 February 2007 contract assignment the Bank took over the unpaid debt of EUR 16,920,000 to the supplier, and under a business-technical cooperation contract of the same date it undertook to pay the Ministry EUR 8,030,000 for sums the Ministry had already paid. A commission formed during the audit by a vice-governor's decision confirmed that the equipment was not fully put into use although depreciation had been charged against expenses the whole time, and that part of the equipment the Ministry received from the supplier (Basin for manual coating and ESC Drying rack model) was never delivered to the Bank. The auditor records that the Bank nevertheless paid the Ministry the whole EUR 8,030,000 without reducing it for the undelivered items; the equipment's book value at 31 December 2012 was 24,128 thousand dinars. The audit opinion itself was unmodified.
records.detail: This is the seventh of nine per-entity State Audit Institution reports on the National Bank of Serbia (audit subject 1071 in the Institution's final-reports register, financial years 2009 to 2017). It is a separate document from the financial-year 2016 report already on the map and concerns different conduct, different counterparties and different years. The Serbian text reads: 'произлази да уговорене и плаћене обавезе према истом министарству нису умањиване за део неиспоручених средстава'.
records.quote: произлази да уговорене и плаћене обавезе према истом министарству нису умањиване за део неиспоручених средстава
records.source_title: Izvestaj o reviziji finansijskih izvestaja i pravilnosti poslovanja Narodne banke Srbije za 2012. godinu, Drzavna revizorska institucija, no. 400-264/2013-01, Belgrade, 12 December 2013

records.category: procurement irregularity in an open tender
records.people: Radoslav Sretenovic (Auditor General of the State Audit Institution, who signed the report); the winning bidder and the other three bidders are not named in the report
records.summary: In its audit of the National Bank of Serbia for financial year 2014 (report 400-538/2015-07, Belgrade, 9 November 2015), Serbia's State Audit Institution examined the Bank's 387 public procurement procedures worth 3,302,577 thousand dinars and found, in section 2.11 'Public procurement', that in the open procedure for control stickers for the outer packaging of medicines and veterinary medicines (JN 89/2014) four bidders submitted offers but the contract was awarded to the bidder whose samples had been tested earlier, because it was already the supplier of those goods to the Institute for Manufacturing Banknotes and Coins - Topcider. The award rested on an industrial-trials report that the auditor describes as incomplete, because it did not contain essential data on the testing process, together with a written statement from the chosen bidder that it would go on supplying identical goods. The Institution issued Recommendation 2, that the Bank regulate by internal act that the industrial-trials report contain all relevant test data, that sample testing be transparent, that all parameters be known to bidders in advance, and that it prescribe a procedure for controlling the testing process.
records.detail: A separate document in the same per-entity series (audit subject 1071) from the financial-year 2016 report already on the map, and a different finding: a named tender, a stated procurement-law context (Law on Public Procurement, Official Gazette 124/2012 and 14/2015) and its own recommendation. The audit opinions on the financial statements and on regularity were both unmodified.

records.source_title: Izvestaj o reviziji finansijskih izvestaja i pravilnosti poslovanja Narodne banke Srbije za 2014. godinu, Drzavna revizorska institucija, no. 400-538/2015-07, Belgrade, 9 November 2015

records.category: weak controls over the central bank's savings and retirement fund
records.people: Leonardo Ovidio Reyes Ramirez (President, BCN); Sara Amelia Rosales Castellon (General Manager); Victor Manuel Guerrero Alvarado (Manager, Administration Division); Sergio Antonio Martinez (Head of the Programa de Ahorro y Retiro)
records.summary: Resolution RIA-UAI-007-2022 of the Consejo Superior of Nicaragua's Contraloria General de la Republica, adopted unanimously in ordinary session 1265 on 6 January 2022, admits a financial and compliance audit of the Banco Central de Nicaragua's Fondo de Ahorro y Retiro (report IN-014-004-21 of 14 October 2021, covering 1 January 2018 to 31 December 2019) and records three internal-control findings against the Bank: investments were deposited into the fund's savings accounts between one and eleven days after maturity; the fund's information system SIFAR reported incorrect information; and the fund's regulatory framework did not cover activities relating to the 1 per cent retention for management expenses. A recommendation from an earlier audit, IN-014-006-17, was still only 50 per cent implemented. The Consejo established no responsibility against the named officials, ordered the Bank's top authority to apply the outstanding recommendations within 60 days with a further 30 days for any left unapplied, and warned that persistent non-compliance in later audits could give rise to responsibility under article 77 of its organic law.
records.detail: A distinct document and a distinct subject from the procurement resolution RIA-UAI-649-2024 already on the map: a different audit report, a different audited process (the staff savings and retirement fund), a different audited period and a different resolution date. Read through the fetch tool because cgr.gob.ni resets plain curl with no HTTP status. ACCRETION REMOVED on hand check, 17 November 2026: this record first called the Fondo de Ahorro y Retiro the Bank's STAFF savings and retirement fund. The resolution does not say who the fund's members are, so 'staff' was not in the source and has been taken out. The fund is the Bank's; whose savings it holds is not stated.
records.source_title: Resolucion RIA-UAI-007-2022, Consejo Superior, Contraloria General de la Republica de Nicaragua, 6 January 2022

records.category: weak controls over information technology and user access
records.people: No officials are named in the resolution
records.summary: Resolution RIA-119-14 of the Consejo Superior of Nicaragua's Contraloria General de la Republica, issued on 20 February 2014, admits an audit of information-technology management at the Banco Central de Nicaragua's International Division carried out by the Bank's own internal audit unit (report IN-014-025-2012 of 31 December 2012, covering 30 January 2011 to 30 September 2012) and records four internal-control findings against the Bank: problems in the matrix and user catalogue of the production systems; no monitoring or review of audit trails in databases, log files and shared folders; problems in managing the IT equipment and accessories assigned to the division; and an out-of-date technical user manual for the payment interface module of the SIGADE accounting system. The Consejo found no audit findings giving rise to administrative irregularities and established no responsibility against current or former officials, but ordered the Bank's top authority to apply the corrective measures and report within 90 days of notification.
records.detail: Earliest of the Contraloria's per-entity resolutions on the Bank reached this round, a decade before the resolution already on the map, with its own audit report, period and findings. The resolution names no individuals, so none is asserted here.
records.source_title: Resolucion RIA-119-14, Consejo Superior, Contraloria General de la Republica de Nicaragua, 20 February 2014

records.summary: Resolution RIA-UAI-505-2025 of the Consejo Superior of Nicaragua's Contraloria General de la Republica, issued at regular session 1429 on 15 May 2025, admits a compliance audit of how the Banco Central de Nicaragua had carried out the recommendations of earlier approved audit reports (report IN-014-005-24 of 20 November 2024, covering 1 January to 31 December 2023). It records that all Bank areas had submitted implementation timetables, but that the Bank had not implemented any of the four recommendations in audit report IN-014-002-23, approved under resolution RIA-UAI-649-2024, a rate of 0 per cent compliance. The Consejo established no responsibility against the named officials and required the Bank's top authority to report through the SIIRCI system on implementing the unfulfilled recommendations once the timetable fell due.

Anyone merging should keep them distinct or, if a single record is preferred, fold this into the existing one rather than drop it.

records.category: conflict of interest in the central bank's management of assets it had taken over
records.people: The Governor of the Central Bank of Iceland and the Auditor General are referred to by office and are not named on the page (seedlabankastjori, rikisendurskodandi)
records.summary: In its report to the Althingi 'Fyrirgreidsla rikisins vid fjarmalafyrirtaeki og stofnanir i kjolfar bankahrunsins' (June 2012), Iceland's National Audit Office records that in a memorandum of 19 January 2011 from the Auditor General to the Governor of the Central Bank it stated the view that the Governor's sitting on the boards of the companies the Bank owns wholly or largely was inappropriate, because the Bank's management of its statutory tasks must be wholly independent of its interests in asset management. The same chapter records that the Governor was at one and the same time the highest head of the Bank's foreign-exchange surveillance and chairman of the board of the Bank's own private limited company, and that the Bank halted the sale of its stake in the insurer Sjova to a group of buyers because one of them was under investigation by the Bank for breaches of the foreign-exchange rules, completing the sale to the remaining members only after that bidder withdrew; in 2012 the prosecutor dropped the investigation of that person. On the sale process itself the National Audit Office found no grounds for objection.
records.detail: A separate episode from the 2010 parliamentary Special Investigation Commission record already on the map, which concerns 2004-2008 and names David Oddsson, Eirikur Gudnason and Ingimundur Fridriksson. The person holding the office of Governor in 2010-2012 is deliberately not named here, because the report refers to the office only. The PDF cover is dated 'JUNI 2012'; the National Audit Office's own report index gives the publication date as 27 June 2012 (https://www.rikisendurskodun.is/skyrslur/nanar?id=476), which is the second source for that day and month. Icelandic text: 'seta sedlabankastjora i stjorn theirra felaga sem bankinn a ad fullu eda miklu leyti vaeri ohoeppileg'. The same chapter 6 states that the Bank's collateralised lending to the banks stood at 345 billion kronur at end-2008, that 75 billion was written off at once and that the loss of the Bank and the Treasury together was put at 267.2 billion kronur - not filed, because that is the same 2008 collapse episode as the record the map already holds.
records.quote: seta seðlabankastjóra í stjórn þeirra félaga sem bankinn á að fullu eða miklu leyti væri óheppileg
records.source_title: Rikisendurskodun, Skyrsla til Althingis: Fyrirgreidsla rikisins vid fjarmalafyrirtaeki og stofnanir i kjolfar bankahrunsins, June 2012, chapter 6 and chapter 8

records.central_bank: Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten
records.category: governance failures and unusual transactions found by an investigation commissioned by the bank's owners
records.people: The summary names no individuals; it refers to the office of president of the CBCS, the Raad van Bestuur, the Raad van Commissarissen and the finance ministers of Curacao and Sint Maarten
records.summary: A PwC summary report, final draft dated 4 August 2014, of an investigation into the Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten commissioned by the finance ministers of Curacao and Sint Maarten as representatives of the Bank's beneficial owners, covering the Bank's governing bodies from 10 October 2010 to 31 May 2013, found that the Bank's statute gives the president a dominant position with no true collegial governance and too little counterweight inside the executive board; that the supervisory board was stalled for long periods, with a seventh member appointed only in March 2012, disputes over quorum and the validity of decisions, and three members ceasing to attend meetings from September 2012; that no meeting of the Vermogensgerechtigden was held between 10 October 2010 and the report date, contrary to the statute; that the Bank's transactions for the Sint Maarten Harbour Holding bond issue were unusual, conflicted with the monetary and investment policy then in force, and were reported by the executive board to the supervisory board too little and too late; and that the supervisory board had not acted on the investigation into the president. The Minister of Finance of Curacao asked PwC Nederland to propose the investigation on 31 January 2013; fieldwork ran in May and June 2013, findings were presented on 25 November 2013 and the final report was handed over on 17 April 2014.
records.detail: Distinct from both CUW records the map holds: the Emsley Tromp and Rene Laurents convictions (2009-2024) and the Algemene Rekenkamer finding on unlawful state loans (2020-2023, counterparty only). This is a consultant's investigation commissioned by the two finance ministers rather than a report of a state audit institution, so 'official finding' is the nearest accurate status on the closed list and is flagged here as such. The investigators state they did not audit the information they received and give no assurance, and they did not examine individual integrity.
records.source_title: PwC, Rapport Centrale Bank van Curacao en Sint Maarten - samenvatting (final draft), 4 August 2014
records.weak_source_note: HOST, NOT DOCUMENT. The report itself is the primary PwC summary: its cover reads 'Onderzoek CBCS' and '04 augustus 2014', and chapter 4 is the Harbour case, all read directly. The weakness is that no host serves it to a plain request. knipselkrant-curacao.com answers HTTP 404 with a 142,531-byte HTML page ('Knipsel niet gevonden') to curl on both the single- and double-slash path and with a browser user-agent; the adoc.pub mirror at https://adoc.pub/centrale-bank-van-curaao-en-sint-maarten.html answers 403. The text was read through the fetch tool, which serves a cached copy. So a reader clicking this link gets an error page, and the record rests on a document that is no longer publicly served at the address it is cited from. PwC's own copy and a ministry copy were not located. Checked by hand 17 November 2026.

records.category: unauthorised spending out of the Treasury's settlement account at the central bank
records.people: The Tresorier general and the ministers in charge of finance are referred to by office and are not named in the audited passage
records.summary: COUNTERPARTY ONLY - the subject of this finding is Senegal's Treasury and its finance ministers, not the central bank. Senegal's Cour des comptes, Chambre des affaires budgetaires et financieres, in its final audit report on the state of the public finances for the years 2019 to 31 March 2024 (February 2025), found that on 29 December 2023 the Tresorier general transferred 15 billion CFA francs out of his settlement account at the BCEAO into an account opened in his own name at a commercial bank, that the transfer was posted on 2 January 2024 and moved the same day into an account in the name of the State of Senegal at the same bank managed by the minister in charge of finance, and that the money was at once used to pay unauthorised expenditure to various suppliers. The Court also found that the authorisation given to finance ministers to open accounts at the BCEAO or at commercial banks for Treasury funds gave them no licence to handle public money, only accountants being so entitled under article 125 of decree 2011-1880 of 24 November 2011, and that by ordering a financial institution to use a public accountant's term deposits to pay unauthorised expenditure they had irregularly bound the State.
records.detail: Filed as counterparty_only so it shows in Senegal's box without colouring the row. It is the document round 72 named and could not open: courdescomptes.sn answers 404 to curl on both spellings, but the Government of Senegal's own portal serves the identical PDF at the URL given here, which was found from the search-returned landing page www.vie-publique.sn/documents/11286. The whole 160,000-character text was grepped for BCEAO: fifteen hits, of which twelve are account-name rows in the Treasury's bank-statement tables and the rest are the passages used here - no finding anywhere in the report is against the central bank itself.
records.quote: à partir de son compte règlement ouvert à la BCEAO, à un virement d’un montant de 15 milliards de F CFA
records.source_title: Cour des comptes du Senegal, Chambre des affaires budgetaires et financieres, Rapport definitif - Audit du rapport sur la situation des finances publiques, gestions de 2019 au 31 mars 2024, February 2025

blanks: SRB [confirmed blank, five of seven] All seven unopened per-entity reports of Serbia's State Audit Institution on the National Bank of Serbia were downloaded and read (audit subject 1071 in the final-reports register, https://www.dri.rs/konacni-izvestaji-o-reviziji?subjects=1071, which lists nine reports in all and is now fully enumerated: FY2009 2009/izvestaj2009-10.pdf, FY2010 2010/izv-nbs2010.pdf, FY2011 2011/5_nbs2011.pdf, FY2012 2012/5_26122013_4.pdf, FY2013 2013/5-nbs-1.pdf, FY2014 2015/2015-5-nbs-1.pdf, FY2015 2016/Izvestaj...za 2015. godinu.pdf, FY2016 2017/...za 2016...pdf, FY2017 2018/2018-5-NBS_v2.pdf). Two converted (FY2012, FY2014, filed above). The other five are blanks, and each one is a separate checked year: FY2015 (report 400-1185/2016-07/9, 23 December 2016) carries unmodified opinions on both the financial statements and regularity and its two Priority 1 recommendations are the SAME two items as the FY2016 report already on the map - the stocktaking of finished-goods inventories held at the Ministry of the Interior's commission agent, and requiring the contracted collateral instruments from staff loan/credit beneficiaries - so it is the same episode a year earlier and was NOT filed as a second record. FY2013 (400-165/2014-07, 20 November 2014): unmodified opinions, four recommendations, all bookkeeping or software (cost-allocation software, aligning the financial plan with the income statement, finishing an inventory-valuation software upgrade) plus one to settle 748,337 thousand dinars of claims on the Republic under 1995 and 2000 contracts of the former National Bank of Yugoslavia; no irregularity asserted. FY2011 (400-241/2012-01/1, 21 December 2012): unmodified opinions, no emphasis-of-matter paragraph, nothing. FY2010 (400-731/2011-01/1, 16 December 2011): unmodified opinions; the only emphasis paragraph is an accounting-presentation matter - the Bank recorded estimated refining costs for part of its gold reserves as a value adjustment of 36,613 thousand dinars on a four-digit account that also carried quantities, so the gold quantity in the books was 10,185.43 grams lower than the quantity counted at 31 December 2010, which the Bank corrected in 2011 by opening a three-digit account; not filed because the auditor states it does not modify the opinion and it is a presentation defect, but it is the nearest miss of the five. FY2009 (400-364/2010-07/7, 15 December 2010): unmodified opinion; emphasis paragraph records that in distributing the surplus of income over expenses for 2008 and 2009 the Bank treated exchange-rate differences as unrealised income, a deductible item under article 77 of the then Law on the National Bank of Serbia, which the auditor notes the law and subordinate acts did not define, and which the 2010 amending law (Official Gazette 44/2010) then specified; no irregularity asserted, so not filed. The vein named in the assignment is now exhausted: all nine reports have been opened.

ISL [vein closed, performance appraisal] The government's 'Mat a frammistodu Sedlabanka Islands 2020-22' is served with HTTP 520 by fm.mfa.is, but the same appraisal is on the Prime Minister's Office site and two pieces of it were read instead: the foreword and summary of the appraisal panel's report (Pentti Hakkarainen, Patrick Honohan and Joanne Kellermann, January 2023, https://www.stjornarradid.is/library/01--Frettatengt---myndir-og-skrar/FOR/Fylgiskjol-i-frett/Sk%c3%bdrsla%20um%20Se%c3%b0labanka%20-%20form%c3%a1li%20og%20samantekt.pdf) and the November 2021 review committee report on the experience of the Bank's three committees 2020-2021 (https://www.stjornarradid.is/library/02-Rit--skyrslur-og-skrar/Sky%cc%81rsla%20u%cc%81ttektarnefndar.pdf, 180,000 characters, grepped for conflict-of-interest and breach vocabulary). Neither contains a finding of misconduct or irregularity. The 2023 appraisal says the Bank handled the external shocks as well as other European and North American central banks and that staff do their duties as expected; its criticism is of the mandate of the financial supervision committee and of the top-management arrangement chosen after the merger, which is institutional design, not an adverse finding. The November 2021 report notes at one point that one external member the minister appointed to the financial supervision committee is a department head in the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs, which it says could raise questions of disqualification because the Treasury holds stakes in two of the three commercial banks - but it expressly takes no position on that question and makes no finding, so under this round's rules it is not a record. That dual role is the one open ISL lead left and is listed below.

ISL: the one open lead is the dual role noted in the November 2021 review committee report - a serving department head of the Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs sitting as an external member of the Central Bank's financial supervision committee while the Treasury holds stakes in two of the three commercial banks. The committee names nobody and makes no finding, so it needs the minister's own appointment announcement to become a record, and it would belong on the revolving-door or conflict row rather than on cases.
